about: S07.6 (D.8): the Family Hub and Digital Banking tone gate's scope, lexicon and reviewed exceptions. Law 2: speak like a mentor, never like a bank. D.7: no copy may imply a guarantee the system does not enforce. Owner log §5: the controlled glossary. agent/tools/check-family-copy-tone.mjs reads this file; docs/operations/FAMILY-COPY-TONE-GATE.md explains how to change it. An exception needs a reason a reviewer can check.

scope.surfacesWhy: Core's error messages are English developer diagnostics. A family reads only the rebuilt surfaces' own copy, in scope here (the legacy errors.json and common.json tasks/banking subtrees left with the legacy UI in S10L.1). The gate fails if a Family Hub or banking surface starts rendering a raw Core message.

bank_register.why: Law 2: transactional, procedural or legal banking language turns a moment of friction into a bank notice.

guarantee.why: D.7: no copy may promise safety, protection, insurance or a real bank or card that the simulation cannot back.

glossary.why: Owner log §5: coins, never money; a chore is never a job; approve, never accept; rest day, never streak freeze; the verified parent is the Tutor, never a guardian.

shouting.why: Law 2: a mentor never shouts: no stacked exclamation marks, no words in capitals, no raw error codes.

exceptions.why: The S07.3 (D.11) disclosure: a bonus the family adds, not a bank interest rate. Naming what it is not is the honesty line.
The teen's form of the D.11 disclosure: a bonus the family adds, not a bank interest rate.
An adult accepting an invitation to join, not a Tutor approving a chore or reward (the glossary's approve rule).
An adult accepting the teen's invitation, not a Tutor approving a chore or reward (the glossary's approve rule).
A Tutor refusing an adult who asked to join the child's account, a safety decision about a person, not a money transaction.
The D.20 scope statement says no real money moves, which the D.7 control registry backs: coins never leave the app, and the gate fails on any payment, card or bank-linking SDK.
Names real money only to say that none moves; the coins themselves are never called money.
The D.20 scope statement names credit cards as a topic the practice does not teach (Appendix G §3.5).
In es-MX and pt-BR "seguros" means insurance, named as a topic the practice does not teach; it promises no safety.
The D.19 bridge advises a teen about a real bank account outside the app (ask about its fees first); it describes no in-app transaction.
